body: TLS shape: keep the two listeners and wrap each in rustls TLS 1.3 (newline-JSON agent link over TLS, hand-written HTTP/1.1 hooks over TLS = HTTPS) through one Stream enum; rejected one WebSocket listener over HTTPS (new crates, protocol rewrite, hub domain says no WebSocket until a browser client).

Client verification: pin the sha256 of the hub certificate (CCTG_HUB_CERT_SHA256) with a custom ServerCertVerifier that still checks the handshake signature; rejected system/platform roots for a real domain (hub reads its cert once at start, CA renewals would need reload plumbing; pin works for IP-only servers and needs no CA).

TLS switch: a pin set = TLS on both links; without a pin a device talks plain TCP only to a loopback address (refuses remote plain, ConfigProblem::PlainRemote); rejected a tls:// scheme prefix in the address (two knobs for one fact; forgetting it sends the secret in clear).

Build identity: build.rs bakes CCTG_BUILD_ID (CI/Docker) or the git commit (+ -dirty for changes under crates/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock); a dirty build appends the exe sha256, no git falls back to the exe sha256. Rejected vergen (new deps) and a bare <commit>-dirty (two dirty dev builds of one commit would compare equal and hide a stale agent).

One binary with subcommands stays; rejected cargo features/separate server and client binaries (TASK-040 deploy and shim rely on one file per machine, feature gating touches most modules and doubles the CI matrix, the release exe is 10 MB).

Healthcheck: `cctg health` TCP-connects both listeners on loopback and closes without a byte; hub logs such connections and failed TLS handshakes at debug. Rejected an unauthenticated HTTP health route on the public port and a heartbeat file written by the poll loop (more code, needs TLS in the probe or a new hub task).

Updater: optional compose profile with nickfedor/watchtower (maintained fork, label-enable, cleanup) plus documented manual `docker compose pull && up -d`; rejected containrrr/watchtower (archived 2025-12-17).

Image: static musl build on rust:1.95-alpine, runtime alpine:3.21 with uid 10001 and /data volume; the same build stage exports the Linux release binary (--target binary). Rejected glibc + distroless (needs a second Linux build for the static client binary).

An unquoted openssl fingerprint line (`sha256 Fingerprint=AB:..`) as CCTG_HUB_CERT_SHA256 value breaks dotenvy parsing of the whole device.env (the device then has no secret); docs say to paste only the hex or quote the line; the e2e uses the quoted form.

tokio::io::split halves keep the socket open while either lives; the reader task spawned per connection outlived an aborted serve_agents and the agent never saw the hub restart (2 agent tests failed). Fixed with tls::ReadTask that aborts on drop.

Bot API proxy (orchestrator decision 2): keep reqwest's own env proxy handling (HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY), add one start line without the value, compose extra_hosts host-gateway plus compose.host.yml (network_mode host) for a proxy bound to 127.0.0.1; test with a proxy stand-in (CONNECT to a .invalid host, absolute-form requests to a dead loopback port). Rejected: a CCTG_BOT_PROXY variable read from .env (second mechanism next to the standard one).

Linux-only failures of slots_logs and files_e2e (first Linux run, not reproducible on Windows in 15 sequential and 18 parallel runs): treated as ordering races between the actor's agent, hook and control channels; tests wait for the hub's own log line (agent waits for SessionStart / agent bound) before the next event. Rejected: biasing the actor's select! (product change without evidence). Unverified on Linux: Docker was stopped by the user.

Reproducing the missing flush after write_all in hook::post over TLS with one 16 MiB body and a hub reading 500 ms late passed on Windows loopback (the reader drains while the last writes happen); a size sweep 64..512 KiB with a 4 KiB server receive buffer fails at 128 KiB and is the regression test.

macOS client: no process-tree source in this task; nested-run detection, /clear rebinding by claude_pid, live-pid reaping and shim link cleanup stay off on macOS and move to TASK-044 (which now names the macOS parent walk). Alternative rejected here: a libc proc_pidinfo walk that nobody can compile or run before the first CI push.

Pre-auth hardening: one deadline from TCP accept covering TLS plus hello/register (5 s) and TLS plus the whole hook request (2 s), a separate 16-place semaphore for unauthenticated agent connections (excess dropped at accept), hello line capped at 4 KiB via wire::read_line_max, 250 ms pause before answering a wrong secret on both listeners. Rejected: per-IP limits (state and eviction for a single-user hub; documented as residual risk with firewall allowlist / non-default port).

Workflows: third-party actions pinned to commit SHAs (resolved via gh api 2026-09-25), toolchain from the runner rustup instead of dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master, macOS added to the ci matrix and an aarch64-apple-darwin client to release, container smoke (.github/smoke) in the ci image job. Rejected: major-tag pins (mutable).

tests/message_logs.rs polls registry.json until the kept message appears (5 s cap) instead of reading it once after the queued notice: with the patch it failed 4/8 runs (base HEAD 6/6 green) because the slots saver task writes after the notice is sent. Rejected: touching the product save order (the notice does not promise persistence) and blaming the shared target (fails with an unchanged binary).
